transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Thank you for taking the time to see me. I, uh... I hope I'm doing this right, please just stop me if I'm not. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, some folks have been saying my talking gets a little mixed up lately. It's probably nothing major, maybe just a bad habit I picked up, you know? But, like, I'll try to explain something simple—like about my keys at the building I clean—and then... I don't know, suddenly I'm talking about the jail, and then the prayer rug, and then chess pieces. 

It all sort of connects in my head, but people tell me they can't follow what I'm saying at all. I feel awful when I confuse them, I really don't want to be a bother to anyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, it's probably just my imagination playing tricks on me, or maybe the old pipes in the building, you know? I don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. But, um... sometimes, when I'm working, I'll hear this man's voice. 

It usually comes from the vents, or maybe the mop closet. He'll say my name, or... or tell me that I ruined everything. It sounds so real, Dr. Smith, like he's standing right next to me. But then I look, and nobody's there. I try not to let it bother me, I really do. I just keep working. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not sounding too strange.

Have you experienced any periods where you felt so incredibly sad, hopeless, or low that you couldn't function, or perhaps the opposite, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or like you didn't need to sleep for days at a time?

Um, well... I really try to stay positive, you know? I don't want to complain, because I know a lot of folks have it much harder than I do. But... I guess I do have some bad days. It's probably just normal sadness, right? Everybody gets down sometimes. 

But, um... on those days, after my morning prayer, I just... I sit on the edge of the bed. And I feel so heavy, like... like I'm made of lead. And just empty inside. It feels like there's no point in even cleaning myself up or going outside to work. I just sit there. I know I should be stronger than that, and I'm really sorry if it sounds like I'm just being lazy. I try my best to push through it. Is that... does that answer your question okay, Dr. Smith? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
When you have these periods where you feel so heavy and empty, do you hear that man's voice more often or more intensely during those times, or does it happen regardless of your mood?

Um, well... I guess it happens... kind of all the time? I mean, I hope that's the right answer. I don't want to make a big deal out of it. It's probably just me being overly sensitive, you know?

But, um... even when I'm having a good week—well, not a good week, but a calm week, I guess? Like, when I'm not feeling so heavy and sad, and I'm not feeling too... too energetic either. Just... normal. Even then, um, for a couple of weeks at a time, I still hear him. The man in the vents. And... and I also get this feeling that the people in the building are, like, signaling to each other about me. 

I know it sounds silly, and I'm really sorry if I'm wasting your time with this. I try to ignore it, I really do. I just keep my head down and do my job. Is that... is that helpful, Dr. Smith? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Looking back at the past few months, have you ever experienced the voices and the feelings of people signaling you for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed or particularly energetic?

Oh, um... yes, Dr. Smith. I think I might have just mentioned that, but I'm so sorry if I wasn't being clear enough before. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer. 

But yes, um... looking back over the last few months, there have definitely been calmer weeks. Times when I wasn't feeling all heavy and deeply sad, and I wasn't feeling too wound up or high-energy either. Just... regular, I guess. But even during those regular times, for, yeah, more than two weeks straight... I still heard the man in the vents. And I still believed the people in the building were signaling about me. 

I try not to let it get in the way of my cleaning, though. I just keep my head down, like I said. I promise I still do a good job. Is... is that exactly what you were looking for? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

Thinking about the entire time you've been struggling with these experiences, have your moods—the times you feel very low or very high—ever lasted for a significant portion of the total time you've been ill, compared to the times you feel 'regular'?

Um, well... I really want to be helpful, Dr. Smith, so I hope I'm understanding you right. I don't want to make it sound like I'm always out of sorts, because I really do try to stay on top of things. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and looking at the whole time since all this started... I guess most of the time, I've been in those... those really keyed-up stretches. The times when I'm just... talking way too much, and I get these huge ideas for cleaning the whole building that I could never actually finish. I just feel so driven, like... like I physically can't slow down. 

I know that probably sounds like I'm hard to be around, and I'm really sorry if I am. I don't mean to be a bother to anyone. I just... I get so wound up. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you need from me.
